stories.detail: Cam Skattebo missed a fourth straight practice on Friday due to his hamstring injury, but the New York Giants are not ruling their leading rusher out for Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Skattebo is officially considered doubtful. “Let’s see what happens” head coach John Harbaugh said of Skattebo’s status. Wide receiver Malik Nabers , who missed practice on Thursday, yelled to reporters that he practice on Friday . Harbaugh said that Nabers’ health is “not an issue” for Sunday. If Skattebo cannot play, Devin Singletary will be the Giants’ primary running back against the Eagles. Gregory Desrosiers is the other back on the 53-man roster, and Phil Mafah and Eric Gray are on the practice squad. The other injury of note for the Giants involves wide reciever/returner Charlie Jones . He turned up on the injury report this week with a hand injury, and is listed as questionable. “He’s managing it,” Harbaugh said. “He was out today catching and everything like that. stories.title: Saquon Barkley set to play as Eagles remain without DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks
stories.summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is on track to play against his former team.
stories.detail: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is on track to play against his former team. Barkley remained limited in practice on Friday with hamstring and back injuries, but he has no injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. Barkley missed a couple of games with the hamstring injury and has been limited to 32 offensive snaps the last two weeks. While quarterback Joe Milton will have Barkley with him in the backfield for his first Eagles start, he'll be missing wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Smith and Wicks are both going to miss their third straight game. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring, quad), defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), wide receiver Britain Covey (knee), and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have also been ruled out. Tanner McKee, who was benched in favor of Milton this week, is questionable with a rib injury. Cole Payton is the other quarterback on the 53-man roster.

teamStories.detail: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders starting cornerback Darien Porter is questionable to play Sunday at the San Francisco 49ers, coach Klint Kubiak said Friday. Porter injured his groin on the first defensive play of the Raiders’ 38-33 victory at the New York Jets on Sunday. He didn’t practice Wednesday, but did work on Thursday and Friday. If Porter can’t play Sunday, kickoff is 1:25 p.m. PT, rookie draft picks Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses will rotate as they did in Week 8. Meanwhile, veteran backup defensive tackle Thomas Booker is out with a foot injury. He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday. The absence of Booker won’t change the Raiders’ rotation at defensive tackle much against San Francisco.

teamStories.detail: The San Francisco 49ers host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium. The focus on this used to be bragging rights for Raider Nation vs. Niner Gang as both teams were Bay Area rivals until the Raiders moved to Las Vegas. In the grand scheme of things, it’s just another game on the schedule for both teams. However, it’s a bigger game for the Raiders than the 49ers, as the Raiders need a statement win against a top team. Bringing a (4-4) record back to the Bay is cool and all, but for a fringe team on the outside looking in, it’s a measuring stick. Head coach Klint Kubiak is no stranger to playing and defeating the 49ers, but he is also a member of the Kyle Shanahan coaching tree. Black O vs Red D The strength of the Raiders is in their offense, specifically their passing game. stories.title: Inside LeBron's first game in Philly -- more than two decades ago
stories.summary: Nearly 25 years ago, LeBron won over Philly for the first time -- inside one of the most iconic basketball arenas in the world.
stories.detail: THE FAX LAID out a grandiose plan. Jeremy Treatman, a former high school assistant coach in the Philadelphia suburbs who was running a burgeoning company that staged big-time basketball events between the game's future stars, had just sent a message to Dru Joyce II, the new coach at St. Vincent-St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio, the school famously led by one of the most highly touted prep prospects in the history of the sport. It was the summer of 2002. Six months after a then-17-year-old LeBron James had appeared on the cover of Sports Illustrated accompanied by the headline, "The Chosen One," Treatman was pitching Joyce on choosing him to build James' hype even more. How would you like to play at the Palestra in Philly? How would you like to play Madison Square Garden against Sebastian Telfair? How would you like to play at Ohio State? How would you like to play at University of Dayton? How would you like to play in the Dean Dome in North Carolina? In Philly parlance, Treatman had him at, "Yo." stories.summary: The Knicks have come to the defense of Taylor Swift and say they are "incredibly appreciative" of her support after Tyler Kolek and Miles "Deuce" McBride named her as the fakest celebrity fan at games.
stories.detail: The Knicks have come to Taylor Swift's defense and said they are "incredibly appreciative" of her support after two New York players questioned whether she is a fake fan. During an NBA 2K League livestream posted on YouTube on Thursday, Tyler Kolek and Miles "Deuce" McBride were asked who was the fakest celebrity fan they had seen courtside at an NBA game. "At the Knicks games, I would say it's very performative because like they just want to be seen at the game. They're not necessarily fans. Probably Taylor Swift," Kolek answered and McBride agreed. Kolek acknowledged he was "going to get some hate from the Swifties" before adding "I guess she's got a lot going on, so she can't come all the time, but ... it's a little performative." McBride called other celebrity Knicks fans "solid," naming Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan as examples. On Friday, a Knicks spokesperson responded to the players' comments in a statement. "Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization," the spokesperson said. stories.title: Knicks defend Taylor Swift's fandom after Tyler Kolek, Miles McBride weigh in
stories.summary: Swift's history at Madison Square Garden includes courtside appearances dating back to 2014 and her July wedding to Travis Kelce.
stories.detail: Taylor Swift's New York Knicks fandom is up for debate -- and the team itself has already weighed in. In an NBA 2K League video shared Thursday, Knicks guards Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride were asked to name the "fakest" celebrity fan they'd seen courtside at an NBA game. Kolek floated Swift's name, and McBride agreed. "Maybe Taylor Swift? I don't know if I've seen her at any other games," Kolek said of the pop star's appearance at Game 4 of the NBA Finals . Kolek acknowledged that Swift's schedule might keep her from getting to Madison Square Garden regularly, but he still referred to her fandom as "a little performative." McBride pointed to two familiar faces at the Garden -- Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan -- as examples of "solid" celebrity fans. The Knicks, meanwhile, had a different read on Swift's courtside credentials. "Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization," the team said in a statement to TMZ . Swift has been photographed at Knicks games as far back as 2014, seven years before McBride joined the team and a decade before Kolek did. She was last se…
